prompt: Seller: LifeCore, from the competition brief. It gives employees access to a network of gyms, studios, pools, and wellness classes through one membership and is expanding from individual consumers into employer packages. Do not invent network coverage, pricing, integrations, reporting features, or health outcomes. Prospect: Northstar Software, explicitly fictional. Buyer: People & Benefits leadership. Scenario inputs, not public facts: a main office, a smaller second office, and remote employees; a current gym arrangement centered on the main office. Task 1 universe: employers with distributed teams; actual search filters and company data are not supplied. Task 2 hypothesis: employee routines and geography could make an office-centered benefit less useful for some groups; this is not proof of low uptake or poor wellbeing. Task 3 logic: People & Benefits owns the benefit decision. Public evidence and comparable-company history: none supplied; do not fabricate reviews, success stories, or benchmarks. Create a coverage-first wellness decision brief in the six-part format. Include a practical access check by employee group, an opt-in pilot checklist, and a comparison of the current gym arrangement, an allowance, local memberships, and LifeCore as one alternative. CTA: offer to walk through a coverage comparison and possible pilot. Mark the fictional example clearly. No gift approved. No real prospect logo or domain supplied.
